chunks: And from him, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"Whoever catches the 'Jam' (combined Hajj and 'Umrah), has indeed caught Hajj."

He said, and Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "Any pilgrim who is bringing the offering (saiqin lil-hady), or performing Hajj al-Mufrid, or performing Hajj al-Tamattu' (with 'Umrah) — if he arrives and Hajj has passed for him, let him make it an 'Umrah, and Hajj is due from him next year."

key_terms.سَائِقٍ لِلْهَدْيِ: One who brings/leads the sacrificial animal (a type of pilgrim)
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعٍ بِالْعُمْرَةِ إِلَى الْحَجِّ: One who performs 'Umrah first and then Hajj (Hajj al-Tamattu')
key_terms.مُفْرِدٍ لِلْحَجِّ: One who performs Hajj alone, without 'Umrah (Hajj al-Mufrid)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who misses the Hajj rituals but is still in Mecca?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the legal status of pilgrims who miss the core Hajj rites while still in Mecca, establishing that their presence in the state of Ihram suffices to count as having performed Hajj. It further details the procedural conversion of their current ritual into 'Umrah and imposes the obligation to return for Hajj the following year, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the continuity of pilgrimage obligations. This ruling underscores the jurisprudential distinction between the essential pillars of Hajj and the supplementary rituals, ensuring that pilgrims do not lose the reward of their journey entirely due to timing issues.
